title: Black Forest Labs: FLUX 3 Takes Visual AI into Robotics
summary: Black Forest Labs releases FLUX 3 to bring advanced visual AI capabilities into robotics
detailed: Black Forest Labs is a Freiburg-based visual AI company founded in 2024 by the pioneers of latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion, operating with a team of around 100 people.

The company raised a US$308m Series B co-led by Salesforce Ventures and AMP at a US$3.25bn valuation, taking total funding past US$450m, alongside reaching over US$100m by 2026 and signing a multi-year Meta contract worth about US$140m.
Key partners and customers include Meta, Adobe, Canva, Microsoft, ASUS, Envato, Audi, and mimic robotics.

The company launched the FLUX 3 family, a unified architecture trained across images, video, and audio, including FLUX-mimic for robotic manipulation that requires only 30 minutes of robot data for fine-tuning.

This matters because Black Forest Labs combines open-weight community distribution with closed enterprise licensing (split 50/50), expanding its visual models from cloud enterprise tools like Azure AI Foundry down to consumer hardware like ASUS ProArt laptops.
sentences: A modest team of around 100 people in Freiburg, on the edge of Germany's Black Forest region, supplies image models to the likes of Meta, Adobe, Canva and Microsoft, with its founders' models having been downloaded more than 500 million times.
The group that pioneered the concept of latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion has spent less than two years turning that research pedigree into a business valued at more than US$3.25bn.

That business is Black Forest Labs, and leading the way for the company is Robin Romach, CEO and Co-Founder: “We place vision at the centre of our approach because it is the most signal-rich medium of the physical world,” he says.

“Images convey structure, images and video teach spatial relationships, video teaches dynamics and actions reveal causal relationships.”
In 2024, the researchers behind the latent diffusion method of gen AI and the first-generation Stable Diffusion models founded Black Forest Lab with the goal of creating frontier visual AI models.
It is this wealth of knowledge and models which informs Black Forest Labs’ strategy, which mixes open and closed releases.

Open-weight models build a developer following, while paid API access and enterprise licences generate revenue: the split between usage-driven products and classic enterprise licensing is roughly 50/50.

We place vision at the centre of our approach because it is the most signal-rich medium of the physical world
The commercial traction is significant for a European AI start-up from a relatively small city.

By 2026, the company reached more than US$100m, and had signed a multi-year contract with Meta worth about US$140m – proving that you need not live in a metropolitan city to take roots in the world of AI.
The company has also the company raised a US$308m Series B co-led by Salesforce Ventures and AMP at a US$3.25bn valuation, taking total funding past US$450m.
Backers include a16z, NVIDIA, General Catalyst, Adobe Ventures, Figma Ventures and Canva, several of which are also customers or distribution partners.

Distribution is the other half of Black Forest Labs’ impressive growth story: the company’s FLUX suite of image-generation models combines diffusion with transformers, building on the work from Stable Diffusion.

FLUX.1 Kontext powers Generative Fill in Photoshop beta and Adobe Express, Microsoft offers FLUX.2 [pro] through Azure AI Foundry and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B ships preloaded on ASUS ProArt laptops, the first FLUX model on consumer hardware.
Additionally, Envato has generated more than 51 million images with FLUX, which now accounts for about a quarter of its image volume.
The FLUX 3 family, however, marks a change of ambition from Black Forest Labs.
Rather than separate models for stills and motion, Black Forest Labs trained one architecture across images, video and audio, arguing that each modality strengthens the others.
“True intelligence means perceiving the world: predicting how it will change, taking action and learning from the results.
The most striking application is perhaps its physical AI.

With Swiss start-up mimic robotics, the company built FLUX-mimic, a video-action model for robotic manipulation that can be fine-tuned for a new task with as little as 30 minutes of robot data, against 30 or more hours for earlier approaches.
Audi's Production Lab is testing and deploying it in manufacturing and logistics.
“Joint training within one unified architecture is what will get us [to true intelligence], because each training modality strengthens the others.
“Audio conveys timing, prosody and physical events that elude vision.

Language conveys goals, abstractions and instructions that pixels cannot easily express.”
Adobe FLUX.1 Kontext [pro] is available in Photoshop beta's Generative Fill, Project Concept and Adobe Express, and Adobe Ventures is an investor, placing Black Forest Labs' editing models inside widely used professional design tools.

Microsoft FLUX models are offered through Azure AI Foundry, where FLUX.2 [pro] costs $0.03 for the first megapixel, giving Microsoft's enterprise customers direct access to Black Forest Labs' image generation and editing models.
ASUS FLUX.2 [klein] 4B ships preloaded on ASUS ProArt laptops, the first FLUX model on consumer hardware, targeting image generation in under five seconds on machines with 8GB of VRAM.
